mass_units: rho_mean = 1 per unit area, box mass = L^2 = 4000000.0
particle_ids: a particle's index in every snapshot file is its stable ID = lattice index i (q = ((i % lattice) + 0.5, (i / lattice) + 0.5) * box/lattice)

dm.transfer: T(k) = [1 + (alpha k)^(2 nu)]^(-5/nu), P_WDM = T^2 P_CDM (Viel et al. 2005), same phases as CDM
dm.M_hm_definition: rho_mean * pi * (lambda_hm/2)^2 with rho_mean = 1, lambda_hm = 2 pi / k_hm

spectrum.definition: P0_CDM(k) = A k^n exp(-(k R_c)^2) at a_init (k in 1/box-length-units); WDM multiplies by T(k)^2

normalization.sigma_tophat_host_a1_definition: continuum integral of the linear P(k) from k = 0 (the normalisation target)
normalization.sigma_tophat_host_a1_in_box_definition: same top-hat, summed over the modes present in the periodic box (|k| >= 2 pi/L); this is the variance actually realised
normalization.reasoning: A and a_init are set so that (1) the linear rms density contrast in a 2D top-hat containing 1e6 particles reaches 1.15 at a = 1 when P(k) is integrated from k = 0. CORRECTION: the periodic box has no modes below 2 pi/L, so the in-box value is 0.841 (sigma_tophat_host_a1_in_box): 1e6-particle hosts are ~1.5-2 sigma rarer than the k = 0 value suggests and the largest hosts are somewhat below 1e6 particles. The normalisation was kept unchanged so that all models of the experiment are identical except for the WDM transfer function. k_nl(a=1) stays well inside the box, and (2) the rms delta on the mesh at a_init is 0.1 so Zel'dovich ICs start far from shell crossing. n = -1.5 gives sigma(R) ~ R^-(n+2)/2, a hierarchical spectrum with rich substructure; R_c = 0.35 mesh cells keeps power up to near the mesh Nyquist so the WDM cutoffs are resolved; k_nl(a=1) = 0.018 is ~6 k_fundamental, well inside the box.

units.expansion: Einstein-de Sitter: H = H0 a^-3/2, dt = a^(1/2) da / H0

equations: dx/dt = p/a^2, dp/dt = -grad(phi)/a, laplacian(phi) = C delta with C = 3/2 H0^2 (comoving x, canonical momentum p = a^2 dx/dt); linear growth a^2 D'' + 3/2 a D' - C/H0^2 D = 0 => D = a, D_- = a^-3/2
integrator: KDK leapfrog with merged kicks (Quinn et al. 1997): kick factor int dt/a = 2(a2^1/2 - a1^1/2), drift factor int dt/a^2 = 2(a1^-1/2 - a2^-1/2); steps clamped onto snapshot epochs
stepping: uncapped science run: global step dt = sqrt(2 eta eps / A_max), A = |g|/a^3 (comoving acceleration), dln a = a^(-3/2) dt H0, eta = 0.025, growth <= 25%/step, floor dln a = 0.001, ceiling 0.01; floor/over-CFL statistics in run.log

pm.green: phi_k = -C delta_k S(k) / (k^2 W_cic(k)^2), k=0 removed

short_range.split: Gaussian: mesh phi_k exp(-k^2 r_s^2); short range g_pp r_vec/(r^2+eps^2) exp(-r^2/(4 r_s^2)) for r < r_cut, g_pp = C L^2/(2 pi N_p)
short_range.neighbour_search: chaining mesh, cells >= r_cut, GPU counting sort + prefix sum, 3x3 cells

initial_conditions: Zel'dovich from a lattice x lattice particle grid (cell-centred; lattice a multiple of mesh/2); fixed-amplitude Gaussian field |delta_k| = sqrt(P0(k)/L^2) with random phases from a seeded white-noise field (Hermitian), k = 0 and Nyquist row/column zeroed; Psi_k = i k delta_k / k^2 deconvolved by the CIC window, CIC-interpolated to the lattice; x = q + (a/a_init) Psi, p = H0 a^(3/2) Psi / a_init

pk_measurement.binning: log-spaced from the fundamental 2pi/L to the Nyquist pi N/L; mean k per bin; Nyquist row/column excluded
pk_measurement.cadence: every 0.05 in ln a plus at snapshot epochs and a_final
pk_measurement.p_linear: (a/a_init)^2 * <P0(k)> over the bin's modes, P0 including T^2 for WDM

snapshot_format: little-endian: 8-byte magic GSNAP001, u64 count, f32 a, f32 box, count x [f32 x, f32 y] comoving positions wrapped into [0, box), count x [f32 vx, f32 vy] peculiar velocities v = a dx/dt = p/a in box units per (1/H0); record i is particle ID i in every snapshot
notes: 2D cosmology (planar gravity with a 1/k^2 Poisson kernel). Lattice ICs have sub-Poisson noise, so subtracting the Poisson shot noise L^2/N_p under-estimates P at high k until shell crossing. Velocities in snapshots are synchronized with positions (partial kick). A run is complete when the file COMPLETE exists in its directory.
